services.name: Lawn Mowing & Maintenance
services.shortDescription: A clean, sharp lawn every week — without you ever touching a mower.
services.description:
A well-kept lawn is the first thing anyone sees, and keeping it that way through a full growing season is more than just running a mower over it. We handle the whole job on a schedule that fits your property: mowing at the correct height for your grass type and the season, clean trimming around beds, trees, fences, and foundations, edging hard surfaces for that crisp finished line, and blowing every clipping off your walks, driveway, and patio before we leave.

Mowing height matters more than most people realize. Cutting too short stresses the turf, invites weeds, and dries out the soil; we adjust deck height as conditions change through spring, summer heat, and fall. We also sharpen blades regularly — a dull blade tears grass instead of cutting it, which leaves a brown, ragged tip and an open door for disease.

Weekly and bi-weekly schedules are available, and we keep the same crew on your property so they learn its quirks — the soft spot by the downspout, the sprinkler heads to avoid, the gate that sticks. You get a consistent, professional cut and a yard that's done right every visit, not just the first one.
features: Weekly or bi-weekly recurring service on a set schedule
Mowing height adjusted by grass type and season
Trimming and crisp edging on every visit
Full blow-off of walks, drives, and patios — we leave it clean
Same crew each visit, so your property is never a guessing game
Easy seasonal start/stop and skip-week handling

faq.question: How short should my grass be cut?
faq.answer: For most cool-season lawns we keep it around 3 to 3.5 inches and never remove more than a third of the blade in one mowing. Taller grass shades out weeds, holds moisture, and develops deeper roots. We raise the deck in summer heat and bring it down for the final cuts of fall.

faq.question: Do I need to be home for service?
faq.answer: No. As long as we have gate access, most clients are at work when we come through. We'll text or email if anything needs your attention — a broken sprinkler head, a gate we couldn't open, or a section we couldn't reach.

faq.question: What happens if it rains on my scheduled day?
faq.answer: We don't mow a saturated lawn — it rips up the turf and leaves ruts. We'll push your visit to the next available dry day, usually within 24 to 48 hours, and let you know. You're never charged for a visit we didn't make.

services.seoDescription: Reliable weekly lawn mowing, trimming, and edging in {{city}}. Same crew every visit, clean finish, flexible scheduling. Get a free quote from {{company}}.

services.name: Landscape Design & Installation
services.shortDescription: From bare dirt to a yard you actually want to spend time in.
services.description:
Whether you're starting from a blank slate on a new build or finally fixing the tired beds you've walked past for ten years, a good landscape install is about getting the bones right: proper grading so water moves away from your foundation, healthy soil, the right plants in the right place, and a layout that still looks good in five years when everything has filled in.

We handle the full job — design, plant selection, bed prep, and installation. Plant choice is where most DIY landscaping goes wrong: the wrong plant in the wrong spot either dies or outgrows its space and turns into a maintenance headache. We select hardy, climate-appropriate trees, shrubs, and perennials sized for what they'll become, not just what fits in the pot today, and we account for sun, drainage, and how much upkeep you actually want.

Every install includes proper soil preparation, quality plantings, clean bed edging, and a fresh layer of mulch to lock in moisture and keep weeds down. We'll walk you through watering and care for the first season so the investment actually takes root instead of struggling.
features: Full design, plant selection, and installation
Proper grading and soil preparation, not just digging holes
Climate-appropriate, correctly sized trees, shrubs, and perennials
Bed shaping, edging, and finish mulch included
Foundation plantings, garden beds, and full yard makeovers
First-season care guidance so new plantings establish

faq.question: What's the best time of year to install landscaping?
faq.answer: Spring and fall are ideal — cooler temperatures and reliable moisture let plants establish roots before stress sets in. We can install through summer too, but new plantings need closer watering attention. We'll tell you honestly if waiting a few weeks will give you a better result.

faq.question: Will you design it or do I need a separate designer?
faq.answer: We handle both. For most residential projects we design the layout, recommend plantings, and install it as one job so nothing gets lost between a designer's drawing and what actually goes in the ground. For large or complex projects we can bring in a landscape architect.

faq.question: How long until it looks 'finished'?
faq.answer: It looks clean and intentional the day we leave, but landscaping is a living thing. Perennials and shrubs typically fill in over one to three growing seasons. We size and space plantings for how they'll look mature so it doesn't look sparse forever or overgrown in two years.

services.seoDescription: Professional landscape design and installation in {{city}} — beds, plantings, grading, and full yard makeovers. Free design consultation from {{company}}.

services.name: Hardscaping & Paver Patios
services.shortDescription: Patios, walkways, fire pits, and retaining walls built to outlast the house.
services.description:
Hardscaping is where a yard becomes a place you actually live — a paver patio for the grill and the table, a walkway that doesn't turn to mud, a retaining wall that holds back a slope instead of sliding into it, a fire pit that becomes the spot everyone gathers. It's also the part of landscaping that punishes shortcuts the hardest. A patio built on an inadequate base will heave, sink, and separate within a few winters.

We build hardscapes the right way, starting underground where you can't see it: proper excavation, a compacted aggregate base built to the correct depth for our freeze-thaw climate, the right bedding layer, and edge restraint so the field doesn't spread. The pavers or wall block you see are the easy part — the base is what determines whether it's still flat and tight in fifteen years.

We install paver and natural stone patios, walkways, segmental retaining walls, seating and garden walls, fire pits, and concrete landscape curbing. Every project is graded to drain away from your home and finished with proper joint sand and compaction. The result is an outdoor space that looks great on day one and stays that way.
features: Paver and natural stone patios and walkways
Engineered, properly compacted base — built for freeze-thaw
Segmental retaining walls and seating walls
Fire pits and outdoor living spaces
Concrete landscape curbing for clean bed borders
Graded to drain away from your foundation

faq.question: Why do some paver patios sink and shift?
faq.answer: Almost always an inadequate base. If the gravel base is too thin, not compacted in lifts, or installed over uncompacted soil, the patio will settle unevenly and pavers will separate — especially after a few freeze-thaw cycles. The visible pavers are 20% of the work; the base is the 80% that determines if it lasts.

faq.question: Do I need a permit for a retaining wall?
faq.answer: It depends on the wall height and your local code — many areas require engineering and permits for walls over a certain height, often around four feet. We'll tell you upfront if your project needs a permit or engineered design and handle it correctly rather than building something that fails or gets red-tagged.

faq.question: How long does a paver patio take to build?
faq.answer: A typical residential patio runs two to five days depending on size, access, and whether there's grading or wall work involved. Most of the time is in excavation and base prep — the part you don't see but that makes or breaks the job.

services.name: Mulching, Planting & Bed Care
services.shortDescription: Fresh beds, healthy plants, and far fewer weekends pulling weeds.
services.description:
Clean, mulched beds are the single biggest visual upgrade you can make to a property in one day — and they do real work beyond looking good. A proper two-to-three-inch mulch layer holds soil moisture so plants need less water, moderates soil temperature through heat and cold, and dramatically cuts the weed pressure that otherwise eats your weekends.

We handle the full bed refresh: cutting a clean, defined edge, removing existing weeds, light cultivation where needed, installing quality hardwood or dyed mulch at the correct depth, and planting or transplanting shrubs and perennials. Depth matters in both directions — too thin and weeds push right through; too thick or piled against trunks ('mulch volcanoes') and you suffocate roots and invite rot. We do it right.

We also handle seasonal planting: annual color swaps, perennial divisions, shrub installation, and bed redesigns when something has outgrown its spot or just isn't working anymore. The goal is beds that look sharp and stay that way with less work for you.
features: Hardwood and premium dyed mulch installation
Clean, hand-cut bed edging for a defined line
Weed removal and bed prep before mulching
Shrub, perennial, and annual planting
Correct mulch depth — no root-smothering volcanoes
Seasonal bed refreshes and redesigns

faq.question: How often should mulch be replaced?
faq.answer: Most beds benefit from a fresh top-up once a year, typically in spring. Mulch breaks down and feeds the soil over time — which is good — but it also fades and thins, so an annual refresh keeps both the look and the weed suppression working. We'll tell you if a full removal is needed or just a top-up.

faq.question: Is rock or mulch better for my beds?
faq.answer: It depends. Mulch improves soil as it breaks down, holds moisture, and looks warmer — but needs annual refreshing. Rock is essentially permanent and low-maintenance but doesn't feed the soil and can heat up plant roots. For most planted beds we recommend mulch; for low-plant utility areas, rock can make sense.

faq.question: Can you just refresh the edge without re-mulching?
faq.answer: Yes. A crisp, freshly cut bed edge alone makes a property look maintained even when the mulch still has life in it. We're happy to do edging as a standalone service or bundled with your maintenance plan.

services.seoDescription: Mulch installation, clean bed edging, and seasonal planting in {{city}}. Sharp beds with less weeding. Free quote from {{company}}.

services.name: Tree, Shrub & Stump Service
services.shortDescription: Trimming, pruning, and stump grinding — done safely, cleaned up completely.
services.description:
Trees and shrubs are the most expensive and slowest-to-replace things in your landscape, and they're also the easiest to ruin with bad pruning. Topping a tree, over-thinning it, or 'shearing' a shrub that should be hand-pruned causes damage that takes years to show and years more to recover from. We prune for the long-term health and natural form of the plant, not just to make it smaller this week.

Our tree and shrub work includes structural and maintenance pruning, deadwood removal, hedge trimming and shaping, clearing branches off roofs, gutters, and power-line drops, and crown cleaning to improve light and air. We work safely around your home and never leave a hack job — every cut is made at the right place for the plant to heal.

When a tree or stump has to go, we handle removal and stump grinding, taking the grind down well below grade so you can replant grass or a bed over it. We haul away the debris and rake the area clean — you shouldn't be finding wood chips in your lawn for the next month.
features: Structural and maintenance pruning for tree health
Hedge trimming and shrub shaping
Deadwood, storm-damage, and clearance pruning
Stump grinding below grade for replanting
Tree and shrub removal
Full debris haul-off and cleanup

faq.question: When is the best time to prune trees and shrubs?
faq.answer: It depends on the species. Most deciduous trees are best pruned in late winter while dormant; many spring-flowering shrubs should be pruned right after they bloom or you cut off next year's flowers. Light corrective and safety pruning can be done almost any time. We prune by what's right for the plant, not just what's convenient.

faq.question: How deep do you grind a stump?
faq.answer: Typically six to twelve inches below grade — deeper if you plan to replant a tree or install a bed there. We grind out the visible stump and the surface roots flaring from it, then backfill or leave the grindings depending on what you're putting back.

faq.question: Do you handle large or dangerous tree removals?
faq.answer: We handle most residential tree work and removals safely. For very large trees near structures or power lines that require a certified arborist or crane work, we'll tell you honestly and bring in or refer the right specialist rather than risk your property.

services.name: Pressure Washing & Soft Washing
services.shortDescription: Years of grime gone — without blasting the paint off your siding.
services.description:
Pressure washing looks simple until someone etches their concrete, strips paint off their siding, or drives water behind their boards because they used too much pressure on the wrong surface. The skill isn't in the power — it's in knowing how much pressure each surface can take and when to back off the wand entirely.

We use the right method for each surface. Hard surfaces like concrete driveways, walkways, and paver patios get true pressure washing to lift embedded dirt, oil, and tire marks, often with a surface cleaner for an even, stripe-free finish. House siding, soffits, fences, and decks get soft washing — low pressure plus the correct cleaning solution that kills the algae, mold, and mildew at the root and rinses clean without driving water into your walls or tearing up wood grain.

Common work includes house and siding washing, driveways and sidewalks, paver and concrete patios, decks and fences, and getting that green and black organic growth off the north side of everything. We protect plantings, rinse them down before and after, and leave the property clean.
features: Surface-correct method — true pressure vs. low-pressure soft wash
House siding, soffits, and fence cleaning
Driveways, sidewalks, and patio cleaning
Deck and wood cleaning without grain damage
Algae, mold, and mildew treated at the root
Landscaping protected and rinsed before and after

faq.question: Will pressure washing damage my siding?
faq.answer: It can, in the wrong hands. Vinyl, painted, and fiber-cement siding should almost never be hit with high pressure — it drives water behind the boards and can crack or strip the surface. We soft wash siding: low pressure plus a cleaning solution that kills the growth so it rinses off gently and stays clean longer.

faq.question: Why does the mildew come right back after some companies wash?
faq.answer: Because they only blasted off the surface layer with water and never killed the organism. Soft washing with the proper solution kills the algae and mildew at the root, so it stays clean noticeably longer than a water-only blast.

faq.question: Do you do driveways and patios too?
faq.answer: Yes. Concrete and pavers can take real pressure, and we use a surface cleaner attachment for an even, stripe-free result that lifts oil, tire marks, and ground-in grime instead of just wetting it.

services.name: Spring & Fall Cleanups
services.shortDescription: Reset your property at both ends of the season — the heavy lifting we'll handle.
services.description:
The two cleanups that bookend the growing season are the ones that make every other service look good. A thorough spring cleanup clears out winter's damage and debris so the lawn and beds can wake up clean: dethatching matted turf, clearing leaves and fallen branches, cutting back perennials and ornamental grasses, edging and re-defining beds, and the first sharp mow of the year. It sets the tone for the whole season.

The fall cleanup is the one that protects your investment over winter. A thick mat of wet leaves left on a lawn smothers and kills it in patches by spring, and matted debris in beds invites rot and rodents. We do a full leaf removal and haul-off, cut perennials back, clear and prep beds, do the final season mow at the right height, and leave the property buttoned up for winter.

We haul everything away — you're not left with a pile of bagged leaves and brush by the curb for a month. These are available as one-time services or built into a season-long maintenance plan.
features: Full leaf removal and haul-off — not just blown to the curb
Spring dethatching and bed reset
Perennial and ornamental grass cut-back
Bed re-edging and pre-season prep
Final-cut and winter-prep mowing
One-time or built into a maintenance plan

faq.question: Do I really need a fall cleanup if I mulch my leaves?
faq.answer: Mulch-mowing a light leaf drop is fine and even good for the lawn. But a heavy drop — especially from maples and oaks — mats down when it gets wet and snowed on, smothering the grass underneath. By spring you'll have dead patches that cost more to repair than the cleanup would have.

faq.question: When should spring and fall cleanups happen?
faq.answer: Spring cleanup is best once the ground has firmed up and the threat of heavy snow is past — timing varies by year. Fall cleanup is best after the bulk of the leaves are down but before lasting snow cover. We watch the season and schedule it at the right window, not just a date on a calendar.

faq.question: Can the cleanup be part of my regular service?
faq.answer: Yes — most maintenance clients fold spring and fall cleanups into their seasonal plan so it's handled automatically and priced as part of the package. You can also book either one as a standalone job.

services.name: Snow & Ice Removal
services.shortDescription: Plowed, shoveled, and salted before you back out of the garage.
services.description:
When the snow flies, you want to know it's handled without having to call anyone or stand in the driveway with a shovel before work. We run snow and ice removal as a managed service for both residential and commercial properties: we watch the forecast, we deploy on a defined trigger depth, and we clear your property on a route built to get everyone done fast.

Residential service covers driveways, walks, and steps — plowed or shoveled and treated so you and your visitors aren't walking on a sheet of ice. Commercial service covers lots, drive lanes, sidewalks, and entrances, with the documentation and reliability that property managers and businesses need to stay open and stay liable-safe.

We offer flexible billing that fits how you actually use it — per-push, per-event, per-season contract, or per-inch — so you're not overpaying in a light winter or exposed in a brutal one. Salt and ice-melt application is available as part of the service or on call. You'll know your property is on the route before the first flake.
features: Residential and commercial snow removal
Forecast-monitored, trigger-depth deployment
Driveways, walks, lots, and entrances
Salt and ice-melt application
Flexible billing: per-push, per-event, per-season, or per-inch
Priority routing so you're cleared before you need to leave

faq.question: At what snow depth do you come out?
faq.answer: We deploy on a defined trigger depth — commonly two inches for residential and often lower for commercial lots where liability and access matter more. We set the trigger with you when you sign up, and during big storms we'll make multiple passes rather than waiting for it all to fall.

faq.question: What's the difference between per-push and seasonal billing?
faq.answer: Per-push bills each time we clear the property, so a light winter costs less. A seasonal contract is a flat price for the whole winter regardless of snowfall — predictable budgeting and you're covered no matter how bad it gets. We'll help you pick based on your property and risk tolerance.

faq.question: Do you handle salting and ice control too?
faq.answer: Yes. Plowing clears the snow but doesn't address the ice layer underneath or refreeze afterward. We apply salt or ice melt to drives, walks, and entrances as part of the service or as a separate call, which matters most for commercial properties managing slip liability.
